questions.statement: Which word is the opposite of "young"?
questions.context: La abuela de Martín vive en Santa Rosa de Cabal y cumplió 80 años el mes pasado.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Tall describes height, and its opposite is short, not young.
Incorrect. Happy describes a feeling, and its opposite is sad.
Correct. Young means with few years and old means with many years, so they are opposites.
Incorrect. Short describes height or hair length, not age.

questions.explanation: "Young" significa joven y su opuesto es "old", viejo o mayor. "Tall" y "short" hablan de la estatura y "happy" de un sentimiento, no de la edad.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Mario is 1 meter tall. His dad is 1.80 meters tall. Complete: "Mario is ____ and his dad is tall."
questions.context: Mario mide un metro y su papá, que trabaja en Pasto, mide un metro con ochenta.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Old describes age, and the sentence compares how tall they are.
Incorrect. Curly describes hair with curls, not the height of a person.
Correct. Mario is 1 meter and his dad is 1.80 meters, so Mario is short.
Incorrect. Long describes hair or objects, and we do not say a person is long.

questions.explanation: Mario mide menos que su papá, por eso decimos que Mario es bajo, "short", y su papá es alto, "tall". Para personas no usamos "long": esa palabra es para el cabello o los objetos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Juliana vive en Neiva y su cabello le llega hasta la cintura.

options.feedback: Correct. We use has with he or she to talk about hair: she has long hair.
Incorrect. We say she is tall, but for hair we use has, not is.
Incorrect. Have is for I, you, we and they; with Juliana (she) we use has.
Incorrect. Are is a form of to be for you, we and they, and hair needs has.

questions.explanation: Para describir el cabello usamos el verbo tener: "has" con he o she. Decimos "She has long hair" (ella tiene el cabello largo). Para la estatura sí usamos "is": "She is tall".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word describes hair with many curls?
questions.context: Valeria es una niña de Buenaventura con el cabello lleno de rizos.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Straight hair has no curls; it is the opposite of curly.
Incorrect. Long tells how much hair there is, not if it has curls.
Incorrect. Short tells the length of the hair, not if it has curls.
Correct. Curly hair is hair with many curls.

questions.explanation: "Curly" significa crespo o rizado, con muchos rizos ("curls"). "Straight" es liso. "Long" y "short" solo dicen si el cabello es largo o corto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "My brother Daniel is 12 years old. He is tall and he has short black hair. He smiles a lot."
Which sentence describes Daniel?
questions.context: Daniel es el hermano mayor de Paula y viven juntos en Montería.

options.text: He is short and has long hair.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says Daniel is tall and has short hair, the opposite of this.

options.text: He is tall and has short hair.
options.feedback: Correct. The text says "He is tall and he has short black hair".
Incorrect. Daniel is 12, so he is young, and he smiles a lot, so he is not sad.
Incorrect. The text says his hair is short and black, not blond.

questions.explanation: La lectura dice que Daniel es alto ("tall") y tiene el cabello corto y negro ("short black hair"). Como sonríe mucho, está feliz, y con 12 años es joven, no viejo.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: La profesora de un colegio de Yopal pide a los niños escribir una frase sobre su papá.

options.feedback: Correct. He + is + adjective is the correct way to describe height.
Incorrect. We use has with things like hair; for height we use is: he is tall.
Incorrect. Are goes with you, we and they; with he the verb is is.
Incorrect. For hair we use has: he has long hair, not he is long hair.

questions.explanation: Para la estatura usamos "is": "He is tall". Para el cabello usamos "has": "He has long hair". Con "he" nunca usamos "are".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Carla is happy. She has long curly hair. Sofia is sad. She has short straight hair."
Who has short hair?
questions.context: Carla y Sofia son primas de Barrancabermeja y hoy están en la fiesta de la familia.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Carla has long curly hair, so her hair is not short.
Incorrect. Only one cousin has short hair, because Carla's hair is long.
Incorrect. The text says Sofia has short straight hair, so somebody has short hair.
Correct. The text says Sofia has short straight hair.

questions.explanation: En la lectura, Carla tiene el cabello largo y crespo ("long curly hair") y Sofia tiene el cabello corto y liso ("short straight hair"). Por eso la que tiene cabello corto es Sofia.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
A boy says: "Please find my sister. She is young and short, and she has long hair."
Who is his sister?
questions.context: En un parque de Envigado, un niño busca a su hermana menor entre muchas personas.

options.text: a tall woman with short hair
options.feedback: Incorrect. His sister is short and has long hair, and this woman is tall with short hair.

options.text: a short girl with long hair
options.feedback: Correct. This girl is young, short and has long hair, like the boy says.

options.text: a short girl with short hair
options.feedback: Incorrect. This girl is short, but her hair is short and the sister has long hair.

options.text: an old woman with long hair
options.feedback: Incorrect. This woman has long hair, but she is old and the sister is young.

questions.explanation: Hay que revisar las tres pistas: joven ("young"), baja ("short") y cabello largo ("long hair"). Solo "a short girl with long hair" cumple todas; las otras fallan en una pista.
questions.subject: ingles
